get.summary: Search with intent and clarification questions, the emergency question first (draft)
get.description: Hybrid search plus classification and a rules engine. Behind the `V2_SEARCH_ENABLED` flag; the request and response shapes are a draft until the v2 ADR (ISS-2493).

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Result offset must stay within Elasticsearch max_result_window: page * limit may not exceed 10000 (ES can only return the first 10000 hits), e.g. with the default limit of 25 the highest page is 400.

parameters.name: organization_id
parameters.description: Scope results to resources belonging to a single organization, by its stable organization id (the `organization_id` returned by /suggestion and /organization). Composes with any query_type and with filters.

parameters.name: taxonomy
parameters.description: HSIS taxonomy scope as comma-delimited string or array

parameters.name: geo_type
parameters.description: distance 0 (the default) means no radius filter. Omitted (default): service_area containment AND distance both required (a result with no map point skips the distance check). 'proximity': a result with a map point needs distance only; a result with no map point needs a service_area containing coords. 'boundary': ignores coords/distance, matches service_area against a POST body geometry.

parameters.name: relevance_cutoff
parameters.description: `on` trims low-relevance results; `off` (default) returns the full matched set. The cut uses the dynamic ladder only: 0.2 of the top score, tightened stepwise up to 0.5 when more than 1,000 results would survive, and never below the top-20 scores. There is no `relevance_cutoff_fraction` parameter (ADR 0039 Decision 77). The cut reads scores after the need boost (Decision 58). When a cutoff applies, `hits.total` reports the kept count and `relevance_cutoff.matched_before_cutoff` keeps the original.

parameters.name: coords
parameters.description: Comma-delimited longitude,latitude. Longitude -180 to 180, latitude -90 to 90. Anything else is a 400.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Free text. A repeated parameter or an AND/OR object is a 400.

parameters.name: needs
parameters.description: Confirmed need codes. Repeat the parameter (`needs=A&needs=B`) or send a comma-separated list (`needs=A,B`). They never filter. They boost results and order them in blocks: services with every sent need first, then services with some, then the rest.

parameters.name: passed_needs
parameters.description: Need codes the caller already declined. They are never offered again. Same formats and codes as `needs`: an unknown code or N-X is a 400 that names it.

parameters.name: urgency
parameters.description: Urgency the caller confirmed. `U-X` means not yet known and counts as absent.

parameters.name: clarify
parameters.description: `auto` returns clarification questions. `never` keeps only the emergency question.

parameters.name: classify
parameters.description: `off` turns AI classification off for this request: no need guess and no clarifying question; the emergency check still runs; `needs` and `urgency` sent by the caller still count. It cannot turn AI classification on for a tenant whose setting is off. Name not yet confirmed (draft).

parameters.name: x-tenant-id
parameters.description: NORSE Tenant UUID. On the legacy path it is validated by TenantMiddleware; on gateway-routed requests the same value is also the target-tenant selector checked against the caller's permission slugs by TenantScopeGuard.

parameters.name: x-api-version
parameters.description: Only on `/search`: send `2` to reach this route. `/v2/search` needs no version header.

parameters.name: accept-language
parameters.description: Exactly one supported language code, for example `en` or `es`. It picks the search index. A region tag (`en-US`) or a weighted list is a 400.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: Optional mirror of the resolved accept-language locale, used as a CDN cache-key workaround for edges that ignore Vary headers. If provided, must exactly match the resolved accept-language value or the request is rejected with 400.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: Optional mirror of the x-tenant-id header, used as a CDN cache-key workaround for edges that ignore Vary headers. If provided, must exactly match x-tenant-id or the request is rejected with 400.

200.description: The search answer. A failed classification still answers 200 (`model_version` is null, the emergency question can appear). A failed embedding still answers 200 with keyword results only.

400.description: A header or a query value failed validation, for example a missing or malformed `x-tenant-id`, an `accept-language` that is not exactly one supported code, `limit` under 25, an unknown need code, an unknown `urgency`, or (POST) a Content-Type other than application/json.

404.description: The `V2_SEARCH_ENABLED` flag is not `true`: the route looks absent.

info.title: Norse API: v2 search (draft)
info.description:
Draft contract of `/v2/search`, generated from the code. The main Swagger document leaves it out until the v2 ADR (ISS-2493) is accepted.

Confirmed by David, 2026-11-18 (ADR 0039 Decisions 77-81):
- `relevance_cutoff` uses the dynamic ladder only; there is no `relevance_cutoff_fraction` parameter.
- Classification always runs; there is no `classify` parameter. `clarify` (`auto` or `never`) stays.
- The need boost is on by default.
- For v2 tenants, Norse-API writes tenant scorecard overrides to `sune_scorecard`.
- Payload has a tenant boolean `enableV2Api` (pushed to Redis) and a search engine option `v2`, refused unless `enableV2Api` is on.

applied.description: Whether results were actually removed. `false` means the strategy ran and declined to cut — not that it failed.

reason.description: Why nothing was cut, when `applied` is false. `no_elbow`: nothing scored meaningfully below the threshold, so the distribution is flat and returning everything is the honest answer. `below_min_keep`: the matched set is already smaller than the floor. `cut_too_large`: the cut point was located exactly, but keeps more results than are worth enumerating, so nothing was trimmed — "found it, too big", not "could not find it".

kept.description: Results kept. Equals `matched_before_cutoff` when `applied` is false.

matched_before_cutoff.description: Results the query matched before trimming — the number `hits.total` would have reported with `relevance_cutoff=off`. Kept on the wire because a cutoff hides results rather than reordering them; a consumer needs to be able to say "18 of 1,200 shown".

cutoff_score.description: Score of the last kept result **on the cutoff probe’s scale, which is not the scale of `_score` in `hits`**. The probe ranks on semantic and lexical signal only — it omits the distance decay (0–25 points) and the priority boost that the main query adds — so this value is systematically lower than the score of the same document in the response, and the two must not be compared. It is comparable across responses, which is what it is for: evaluating the shipped threshold retroactively against real traffic.

candidates_examined.description: How many results scored above the threshold — the size of the cut that was located, whether or not it was applied. Counted over the whole matched set, not a fixed window.

see_also_references.description: Related terms: a code and a name each.

taxonomy_names.description: Taxonomy code to display names, per language. Often empty.

attribution.description: Source of the listing, for example a 211 name.

_score.description: Relevance score. null on a text search (the hybrid ranking sorts on a script). A number on a browse (no text).

sort.description: Sort values. Present on a browse (no text): a number, then the result id.

matched_needs.description: Need codes sent in `needs` that this service matches, in sent order. Present only when the request sent `needs`.

max_score.description: null on a text search; the top score on a browse.

state.description: `use` boosts results. `ask` is offered as a question option.

query.description: The typed query when it is a string with text, else null.

taxonomy.description: The `taxonomy` codes the request sent, as sent (not expanded to child codes). Absent when none were sent.

parameter.description: The URL parameter that a pick of this option adds. One question can mix kinds. null (with value null): the pick writes nothing to the URL; the client dismisses the question for this visit (emergency "No, I am safe now").

value.description: The value added to that parameter, for example N-HOU-02 or U-0; null when parameter is null.

results_count.description: Services that match this option; null when the server did not count (all urgency options, and need options when no count ran). A counted option keeps its number. An option with count 0 is never offered.

options.description: Emergency question: "Yes" adds `urgency=U-0`; "No, I am safe now" has parameter and value null (writes nothing); empty for a caller `urgency=U-0`.

hotlines.description: Emergency question only. One tap calls a number.

facets.description: Empty unless the tenant defines facets.

model_version.description: Null when classification was skipped or failed.

message.description: One message, or a list when several validators failed (for example `limit must not be less than 25`).

tenant.description: The tenant id. Absent when the tenant header failed.
